Is it now impossible for time_now and time_previous to be equal (e.g. in a malicious or fuzzed capture file) ?  Is this based on 2 frames not having the same timestamp in them?

This is within 1 frame.
There is a block with 8 timestamps.

It is still possible (code wise) for time_now and time_previous to be equal. However, that will not result in a divide by zero.

See line 710 in that file.

Ok, it was helpful to open the PCAP and follow through the code.

I still don't see how its impossible to avoid dividing by 0, if the Timestamp for 'Sample N' and 'Sample N+1' were identical for a Time Difference of 0.  Should we add an expert info error there and guard against trying to divide by 0?

I don't see how a divide by zero would occur in the latest code.
I've tried it with 2 timestamps being the same and it works like I meant it to; I'll attach the pcap for that.

[IM2R0-timestamps_same.pcapng](/uploads/149fe1b6b42712eb2ccfba827fad958c/IM2R0-timestamps_same.pcapng)

Apologies, I somehow checked and was looking at the previous version.  Thanks for your patience.

That is on purpose. Is was to test the 'others' case in the original commit.
Now a value_string is used, so it is less useful, but for me it was good to see that I still get a value (Unknown) on that value.

In [`print.c`](epan/print.c#L1330-1338), there is this claim:

```
* Do not use gmtime_s(), as it will call and
* exception handler if the time we're providing
* is < 0, and that will, by default, exit.
```

I don't know if that's still true.
I think that it's basically impossible to have negative time above now that we're only supporting 64-bit Windows, so that probably doesn't matter.
I hate Windows...

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9193/diffs?diff_id=567773729&start_sha=ee509cc3f25eacecd60a73da135a2065c34a77d8#93da7cbf00c618476c5f54bd108888f058779c24_508_506)

Fixed this in an easier fashion.
There was actually no reason to use gmtime_r, so I'm just using gmtime.
resolved all threads

I would consider using the Wireshark `nstime_t` type instead of doing the `strftime` and `gmtime`, and also adding the timestamp as a `FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME` type with the appropriate ENC_SECS_NSECS type instead of as a string. `wsutil/nstime.h` has some facilities for subtracting times with nanoseconds. That would mean that you would get a more default time string formatting (with nanoseconds after the decimal point instead of `%9u TAI` as you have here) but I think it could make for simpler code, and it's usually better to use `proto_tree_add_item` (or `proto_tree_add_time`) than add it as a string.

mmm, to me that would not make it simpler.
I tried it a bit and it seems less to-the-point.
Also, it is very important that the timestamp is printed **with** the TAI timezone marker. FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME doesn't seem to know how to do that.

So, for me I'd be quite happy to keep it this way (with the additional commit I just pushed converting gmtime_r to gmtime).
